observation_unit: Work establishment interview record in the 1991 National Organizations Survey (one record per GSS nominator; establishments named by several nominators appear as duplicated records with V3 = 0).
sampling_unit: Establishment, entered through a hypernetwork design: employed respondents (and working spouses) of the 1991 General Social Survey named their employers, so establishments were selected with probability proportional to their number of employees (D1 p5; source description).
assignment_unit: Not applicable (observational cross-section); HRM practices are establishment-level informant reports, not assigned.
clusters: None used by the article. Potential dependence: duplicated establishment records (same interview copied to several nominators) and industries (two-digit SIC groups, absorbed by dummies rather than clustered). The article reports no clustering.
native_se_method: Conventional OLS standard errors (footnote a 'standard errors in parentheses'); no robust, clustered or design-based correction is mentioned. One-tailed t-tests at .10/.05/.01; residual degrees of freedom not printed. Joint tests are incremental F-tests on R2 changes (footnotes c, d).
software: Not stated anywhere in D1 or D2.
first_stage: not applicable (no instrumental variables; the authors state 'appropriate instrumental variables were unavailable', D1 p19)
unavailable_sources: Authors' two-digit SIC assignment for each establishment: the public NOS file contains only 1980 Census industry codes (V43/INDUSTRY); the article does not say how SIC codes were obtained.
Item list for the union pressure index (alpha reported, items never listed).
Recode rule for the decentralized decision making items (NOS multi-category locus codes to the article's 1-5 scale).
Complementarity count-variable regressions and their dummy/spline transformations ('results not shown', D1 p17).
Subgroup analyses by for-profit/nonprofit status ('available upon request', D1 p18).
The set of interaction subsets the authors 'experimented extensively' with (D1 p17).
Sample-construction account from responding organizations to the analysis samples (no attrition table; no missing-data rule).
Degrees of freedom for F-tests; software; any appendix (none exists per the packet search).
vintage_fallbacks: Data vintage: the authors cite the 1993 University of Minnesota/ICPSR release of the NOS (D1 p21 reference list); the available file is ICPSR 6240 V1 (second ICPSR release, November 1994; version date 2006-01-18). The file-creation documentation records that six cases were re-designated as duplicates late in processing, so record counts and duplicate flags may differ from the authors' copy. Fallback: use DS0002 as released and record the duplicate handling (axis A01).

Industry classification: no SIC variable exists in the release; fallback is the study-local transcription of the 1980 Census industry classification with 1972 SIC equivalents (census1980_industry_sic1972.csv), applied to V43/INDUSTRY (axis A17). The authors' 1972-vs-1987 SIC edition is not stated; the 1980 Census list prints 1972 SIC equivalents.

Missing-value declarations: the NOS technical manual states the original SPSS-X file declared no missing values; the ICPSR .por declares user-missing codes for most variables but leaves 997 (application counts) and 4 'varies/depends' (training effectiveness) undeclared. Fallback: apply the dictionary's substantive/non-substantive distinctions explicitly rather than relying on file declarations.
Weights: WEIGHT is documented as RAWWGT rescaled to the distinct-establishment count; the article uses none. Fallback: unweighted (axis A19 L0).
